articles.title: How Seaside House Explores the Relationship Between Brick, Wood, and the Coastal Landscape
articles.summary: Brick and wood can establish a dialogue between architectural permanence and the textures of coastal environments. In Höllviken, on the southern coast of Sweden, Seaside House by Koistinen Hellborg Architects explores how materiality, light, and spatial organization can shape a home in relationship with its natural surroundings. Located among sandy terrain, heathland, moss, and pine trees, and within walking distance of the sea, the house responds to a landscape defined by subtle color variations, seasonal changes, and a strong connection to the outdoors.

articles.title: Small Houses in Uruguay: How Three Studios Build Light on Rural and Coastal Sites
articles.summary: In Uruguay , small-scale residential projects increasingly occupy rural and coastal landscapes, from the hills of Villa Serrana to the maritime forests along the Atlantic coast. Building in these areas often requires structural materials that balance durability, thermal efficiency, and transport feasibility. In these environments, projects rely heavily on materials such as engineered timber framing, steel structural members, exterior wood cladding, or offsite fabrication. These design choices not only help to reduce the weight of raw materials that must be transported over unpaved access roads

articles.title: Villa Sanlomjoy / Yangnar Studio
articles.summary: Rooted in childhood memories, the house began with a collection of salvaged wooden doors and windows, some sourced from Myanmar via Mae Sot, Tak, Thailand. Their character reflects an Anglo-Burmese synthesis, combining British Colonial proportions and European window typologies with traditional Burmese craftsmanship—wooden joinery, pegs, louvers, and casement windows. Rather than serving as decorative elements, these openings became the architectural framework of the house, defining its proportions, height, rhythm, and relationship with light and air.

articles.title: House in Minamigata / Yutaka Yoshida Architect & Associates
articles.summary: This is a small house situated in a corner of a small town located between the Shinkansen line extending from JR Okayama Station and two conventional rail lines. Nearby lies the Nishikawa Greenway, which runs through the heart of Okayama City, and on the north side of the lot, across a waterway, is a small amusement park planted with cherry trees—an environment enveloped by water and greenery.

articles.title: Making Room for Rest in Residential Interiors
articles.summary: Wellbeing is no longer confined to exclusive resorts, spas, or hospitality settings. Today, it has become an essential part of contemporary living, inspiring homeowners to create private spaces dedicated to relaxation and personal care. Collections such as LEMI's Home Spa Collection explore this growing interest in residential wellness through a selection of massage beds and relaxation loungers.

articles.title: 7th door Hangzhou Restaurant / Chakchak Studio
articles.summary: Hangzhou is a historic Chinese city and home to world-class corporations like Alibaba and DeepSeek. Located near "West Lake" in the heart of the city, "Meihuatang" is a registered modern cultural heritage site of Hangzhou.

articles.title: Plaza Pochote Commercial Center / FAMM Arquitectura
articles.summary: Plaza Pochote is a commercial development designed by FAMM Arquitectura in Santa Teresa , Costa Rica. Located along the town's main road, the project responds to a predominantly linear pattern of roadside development and the limited availability of public space within a rapidly growing coastal context. Rather than consolidating the program into a continuous commercial frontage, the architecture separates two built volumes to form an open plaza between them, making the space between buildings the primary organizing element of the project.

articles.title: Bahia House / Patricia Martinez Arquitetura
articles.summary: Conceived as an exercise in synthesis, Casa Bahia, designed by architect Patricia Martinez, head of the firm Patricia Martinez Arquitetura, as a summer home for herself, translates a search for essentiality, where form, materiality, and sensitivity balance in a project that reflects her own vision of architecture.

articles.title: T-237 House / UNO MÁS UNO Arquitectos
articles.summary: Casa T-237 is conceived as a unique architectural piece with a rectangular geometry, resting on the southern boundary of the site and oriented toward a northern courtyard that organizes its relationship with the exterior. With an area of 1,290 sq ft (120 m²), the house proposes a precise response to the essential conditions of living, based on an elementary programmatic organization and a conscious exploration of the expressive and spatial possibilities of the material.
